question.problem: Given that the random variable $Y∼\text{Exp}(\pi ),$ calculate $P(1\le Y\le 3).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $Y$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda y}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
Y∼\text{Exp}(\pi ).
$$

So, $Y$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\pi {e}^{-\pi y}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(1\le Y\le 3)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le Y\le 3) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\pi {e}^{-\pi y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{e}^{-\pi y}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-{e}^{-3\pi }+{e}^{-\pi } \\  & ≈0.0431\end{aligned}
$$
